# Configure a Custom Domain

:::important Alpha Feature
Features described on this page are in alpha and subject to change. For access, contact your Replicated account representative.
:::

Every New Enterprise Portal has a default domain that is always available. You can also add your own custom domain so that customers access the portal at a branded URL.

New Enterprise Portal domains are managed from **Enterprise Portal > Domains**, not from the Vendor Portal **Custom Domains** page. The **Custom Domains** page is used for the Classic Enterprise Portal, the Download Portal, and other Replicated endpoints. For those endpoints, see [Use Custom Domains](/vendor/custom-domains-using).

## Default domain

When your portal is created, Replicated assigns it a default domain in the form `{appSlug}.enterpriseportal.app`. This domain is configured automatically and is always available. It remains available after you add a custom domain, so any links that use it continue to work.

## Add a custom domain

To add a custom domain for the New Enterprise Portal:

1. In the [Vendor Portal](https://vendor.replicated.com), go to **Enterprise Portal > Domains**.

1. Click **Add Domain**. Under **Custom Domain**, enter the domain you want to use, then click **Add**.

    The domain must include a subdomain, such as `portal.example.com`. Root domains are not supported. If you need to use a root domain, contact Replicated support.

1. The domain is added with a **Pending Verification** status, and the Domains tab shows the DNS record you need to create. With your DNS provider, create the CNAME record shown, which points your subdomain at `custom.enterpriseportal.app`. For example:

    | Type | Name | Value |
    | :--- | :--- | :--- |
    | CNAME | `portal.example.com` | `custom.enterpriseportal.app` |

1. After the record propagates, click **Refresh** to check the status. Replicated verifies the DNS configuration automatically, which can take up to 24 hours after your DNS changes propagate.

When verification succeeds, the status changes to **Valid Configuration** and customers can access your portal at the custom domain. The default domain remains available.

## Branding on a custom domain

The login page footer behaves differently depending on whether you use a custom domain. On a custom domain, you can remove the footer entirely. On the default `*.enterpriseportal.app` domain, keeping the footer is recommended to avoid the portal being flagged by Google Safe Browsing. For more information, see [Login page footer](/vendor/enterprise-portal-v2-branding#login-page-footer) in _Customize Portal Branding_.

## Known issue

If you use a custom domain and any of your customers use link transformers such as Microsoft Defender Safe Links, then there is a known issue where legitimate URLs in emails generated by the Enterprise Portal can break due to rewrapping. To avoid this issue, request a "Do not rewrite the following URLs" exclusion policy for your custom domain. For more information, see [Known issue](/vendor/custom-domains#known-issue) in _About Custom Domains_.

## Remove a custom domain

To remove a custom domain, go to **Enterprise Portal > Domains** and remove the domain. After it is removed, your portal is no longer accessible at that domain, and the default domain (`{appSlug}.enterpriseportal.app`) is still available. Update any links or DNS records that you have shared with customers so that they continue to reach the portal.
